### Given Data:
* Box Dimensions: $40\text{ mm} \times 70\text{ mm} \times 50\text{ mm}$ (Width $\times$ Height $\times$ Depth)
* Station Point (SP) distance from Picture Plane (PP) $= 70\text{ mm}$
* Station Point height above Ground Plane (GP) $= 90\text{ mm}$

### General Procedure for One-Point Perspective:
1. **Picture Plane (PP) and Ground Line (GL):**
   * Draw a horizontal Ground Line (GL) and a parallel Picture Plane (PP) line above it at a chosen convenient distance.

2. **Top View Setup:**
   * Place the top view of the rectangular box touching or just behind the Picture Plane.
   * Locate the Station Point (SP) in the top view: $70\text{ mm}$ behind PP, and positioned either $100\text{ mm}$ to the left (Case a) or $100\text{ mm}$ to the right (Case b) of the box's central axis.

3. **Perspective View Construction:**
   * **Vanishing Point (VP):** Since one face is parallel to the Picture Plane, the Vanishing Point lies directly opposite to the Station Point's projection on PP.
   * **Horizon Line (HL):** Drawn parallel to GL at a height equal to the SP's height above the ground ($90\text{ mm}$). VP lies on the HL.
   * **Ray Tracing:** 
     * Draw sight lines from SP to all visible corners of the box in the top view.
     * Drop vertical projectors from the intersection points of these sight lines with the Picture Plane down to the perspective view area.
     * Project heights from the front view (or use height lines touching PP) onto the perspective projection to find the top and bottom edges, converging towards the single Vanishing Point (VP).

4. **Differentiating Cases (a) and (b):**
   * In **Case (a)**, since SP is $100\text{ mm}$ to the left, the perspective view will skew slightly, exposing more of the right-side vertical face of the box.
   * In **Case (b)**, with SP $100\text{ mm}$ to the right, more of the left-side vertical face of the box will be visible.
proTip: In one-point perspective, all lines perpendicular to the picture plane converge to a single Vanishing Point (VP) located on the horizon line.
